title: Singular walking-span bar realization maps weakly to the double mapping cylinder
statement:
Use the simplicial sets, nerves, geometric realization, singular complex and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the Bousfield--Kan construction $\mathrm{BK}_C$ of [lem-coef-bousfield-kan-comparison-calculus]. Let $W$ be the ordinary walking span with objects $a,c,b$ and nonidentity arrows $c\to a$ and $c\to b$ only. For small simplicial sets $A,B,C$ and continuous maps $f:|C|\to|A|$ and $g:|C|\to|B|$, let $V:W\to\mathsf{sSet}$ be the strict diagram $V(a)=\operatorname{Sing}(|A|)$, $V(c)=\operatorname{Sing}(|C|)$, $V(b)=\operatorname{Sing}(|B|)$, with arrows $\operatorname{Sing}(f)$ and $\operatorname{Sing}(g)$, where $\operatorname{Sing}(T)_n=\operatorname{Cont}(|\Delta^n|,T)$ with operators given by precomposition. Put $B_W=\mathrm{BK}_W(V)$, so an $r$-simplex is a chain $i_0\to\cdots\to i_r$ in $W$ with $\sigma\in V(i_0)_r$, i.e. a continuous $\sigma:|\Delta^r|\to|X_{i_0}|$, where $X_a=A,X_c=C,X_b=B$. Let
$$D(f,g)=(|A|\amalg (|C|\times[0,1])\amalg |B|)/((y,0)\sim f(y),\ (y,1)\sim g(y)).$$
For such a simplex and $s\in|\Delta^r|$ put $w=\sum_{j:\,i_j=c}s_j$ and define $\Phi[(i_0\to\cdots\to i_r,\sigma),s]$ to be $\sigma(s)\in|A|$ if $i_0=a$; $\sigma(s)\in|B|$ if $i_0=b$; and, if $i_0=c$, the class of $(\sigma(s),w/2)$ when $i_r=a$, of $(\sigma(s),1-w/2)$ when $i_r=b$, and of $(\sigma(s),1/2)$ when $i_r=c$. Then this formula gives a well-defined continuous map $\Phi_{A,B,C;f,g}:|B_W|\to D(f,g)$, and $\Phi$ is a weak homotopy equivalence: it induces a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on all homotopy groups at every basepoint of $|B_W|$. It is natural for strictly commuting maps of spans, meaning continuous $\alpha_X:|X|\to|X'|$ for $X=A,B,C$ with $f'\alpha_C=\alpha_Af$ and $g'\alpha_C=\alpha_Bg$, acting on $B_W$ through $\operatorname{Sing}(\alpha_X)$ and on $D$ by $\alpha_A\amalg(\alpha_C\times1)\amalg\alpha_B$. Any of $A,B,C$ may be empty.
